agent_response.summary: Candidate 1: share one LU factorization of each frequency's 751x751 signal matrix A. It now serves three solves: the signal solve, the noise-weight solve with A^H (previously a separately factored, materialized conjugate transpose) and the covariance solve. New helpers in differometor/simulate.py are lu_factor, _lu_solve (trans 0/1/2 via lax.linalg.triangular_solve) and solve_factored (lax.custom_linear_solve with matvec A x, or conj(A)^T x for the A^H case). The carrier solve and the public solve() are unchanged. The evidence and proposal are in experiments/notes/claude-linear-algebra.md.
agent_response.hypothesis: Read from source: the baseline factors A^H separately from A in the forward stage (101 complex LUs at n=751, an estimated ~1e11 flops). It may also factor A twice unless XLA CSE merges the signal and covariance getrf calls. The JIT stages save the LUs as AD residuals. Reusing LU(A) for the A^H system (solve via U^H L^H P) should remove at least one LU batch from the forward stage. It should also remove the ~0.9 GB materialized A^H and one ~0.9 GB LU residual. Expected result: lower forward-stage and complete first-run time and lower peak memory. Gradient-stage cost and compile time should be about the same, and the outputs should differ only at rounding level (carrier and signal essentially identical).
agent_response.notes: No local execution was possible (file tools only), so nothing here is measured. Matrix sizes come from the brief plus build.py: CN=286, SN=751 (signal_size 179), 101 frequencies. The off-diagonal sideband blocks are structural zeros, but I have not measured nnz. Derivatives: the operator matvec and its JVP and transpose are unchanged. For M=A^H the transpose_solve computes conj(A)y=b as conj(A^{-1} conj(b)), which is linear in b. The factors are stop_gradient'd, as in jnp.linalg.solve. What to check in the results: (1) whether the screen runs without trace or batching errors; (2) the forward-phase time against the baseline (about 35.74 s first-run); (3) max abs/rel differences in noise, sensitivity, loss and the full gradient against the baseline, plus the official FD gradient check. Diagnostics still needed in a queued follow-up: the count of zgetrf custom calls in the optimized forward HLO (baseline vs candidate), peak RSS, and runtime nnz of the signal matrix. Next step if this helps: a block/Schur decomposition that exploits the zero sideband cross blocks. If it does not help: inspect the HLO to see whether the baseline already deduplicated the factorizations.
